summary: Clarify quota accounting for function-calling + streaming requests (unexpected token burn)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that mixed streaming chat sessions with function-calls are depleting tenant token quota much faster than non-streaming single-shot requests. They see apparent double-counting of tokens and higher-than-expected billing.

Impact:
- Customer hitting hard quota thresholds (P1 business impact) for multiple production routes, causing degraded user experience and automated throttles.
- Billing estimates diverge from observed token burn causing finance/CS escalation.

Environment:
- Prod / us-east-1; tenant uses dedicated+hosted hybrid routing; API keys are per-service.
- Observed across redwood-chat-4k-function-calls model with streaming enabled; large response sizes and frequent function callbacks.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a streaming chat session with function-calling enabled and an open-ended assistant that emits 400-800 tokens across multiple chunks.
2) Trigger a client-side retry after an interrupted chunk (short 100–300ms) and resume/reattach.
3) Repeat with 10 concurrent sessions for 2 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Token consumption logs show spikes aligned with chunk replays and function call acknowledgements; the tenant bucket registers more tokens than sum of raw response sizes.
- Console shows per-route token metrics lower than tenant-level burn.
- Customer sees throttles (~quota-exhausted) and receives P1 alerts.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming vs non-streaming token accounting should match byte/token equivalence; function-calls should only be counted once per logical response.
- Retries/resumes should not double-charge tokens already delivered to the client.

Immediate customer request:
- Request for explanation of how streaming + function-calls + retries are accounted and how to avoid unexpected burn.
- Ask for configuration recommendations (per-route separation, burst sizing, SDK backoff patterns) and a short-term mitigation to avoid more throttles.

Notes:
- Customer provided sample request ids: req-7745ef, req-7745f1, req-7745f2 (attached); and tenant id T-99823.
- They use SDK v2.4.1 with websocket multiplexing enabled and custom reconnect logic.
investigation_notes: Checked tenant-level accounting logs (billing bucket stream) during window 2026-03-09T18:00–18:10UTC; observed 1.9x token burn vs payload-derived estimate.
Per-route metrics (Console) show lower token counts — suggests double attribution at ingress gateway or token counting on both chunk generation and function-call serialization.
Found SDK reconnects that re-request last N chunks using sequence anchors; gateway currently charges tokens for each chunk generation attempt, even if client dedupes on resume.
Hypothesis: Function-calls that emit structured arguments are being serialized twice (assistant -> function -> assistant) and counted at each hop.
Checked recent gateway release notes: commit 4321 updated streaming resume semantics; potential behavioral change in charging semantics.
comments: Support (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged ticket and requested full request-thread logs and SDK reconnect snippet from customer.
Customer (Emma Li, StreamlineAI) 2026-03-10: Uploaded logs and sample client code (websocket reconnect). Notes that retries trigger right after 100–200ms of no data.
SRE (Arjun Patel) 2026-03-11: Replayed requests on staging and reproduced higher token counts when the client re-requested last chunk; attaching replay IDs.
Billing (Nina Ortiz) 2026-03-11: Confirmed tenant-level invoice estimates will reflect actual bucket usage; recommended temporary quota bump to prevent immediate throttles.

Support (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-12: Suggested short-term mitigations: enable per-route isolation for the affected API key, increase burst window for 24h, and apply SDK client-side exponential backoff with jitter on reconnects.
Engineering (Leah Murphy) 2026-03-12: Marked for follow-up; creating internal task to audit streaming resume accounting and add dedupe markers to gateway (INT-74812).
resolution_summary: Workarounds applied: we raised tenant burst allocation by 20% for 48 hours and enabled per-route isolation for the customer's streaming route. Customer applied SDK backoff patch to reconnect logic. Engineering to implement gateway dedupe markers for streaming resumes and to adjust function-call serialization counting; ETA for code change: 2026-03-25.
resolution_status: Workaround in place; engineering fix planned
